title: Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line Module 3 Lesson 2: Meeting Collision Overtaking custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A car travels along a straight road at a constant speed of $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$. As it passes a stationary motorcycle, the motorcycle starts to accelerate uniformly at $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ in pursuit. Find the time taken for the motorcycle to overtake the car.

A motorcycle starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ in pursuit of a car. It overtakes the car after $10\text{ s}$. Find the speed of the motorcycle at the instant it overtakes the car.

Two runners, $A$ and $B$, start at the same instant from points $180\text{ m}$ apart and run towards each other along a straight track. Runner $A$ runs with constant speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and runner $B$ runs with constant speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the time taken for the two runners to meet.

Particle $A$ moves along a straight line at a constant speed of $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Particle $B$ moves along the same line behind $A$, with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and decelerating at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the time at which the distance between the two particles is at its minimum.

Car $P$ travels along a straight road at a constant speed of $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Car $Q$ travels in the same direction at a constant speed of $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and is initially $50\text{ m}$ behind $P$. Find the time taken for $Q$ to overtake $P$.

Cyclist $A$ travels at a constant speed of $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Cyclist $B$ starts from rest at the same starting point $3\text{ s}$ after $A$ departs, accelerating at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Find the distance from the starting point where $B$ overtakes $A$.

questions.prompt: A speeding car passes a stationary police car at a constant speed of $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $2\text{ s}$ after the car passes, the police car begins to pursue it, accelerating uniformly at $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until reaching its maximum speed of $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, which it then maintains.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the time taken by the police car to reach its maximum speed, and calculate the distance between the two cars at this instant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total time elapsed from the instant the speeding car passes the police car until it is overtaken, and calculate the total distance travelled by the police car to the overtaking point.

questions.prompt: Two cars, $A$ and $B$, are initially at rest at points $P$ and $Q$ respectively on a straight level road, where $PQ = 464\text{ m}$. At time $t = 0$, both cars start to travel towards each other. Car $A$ accelerates uniformly at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $10\text{ s}$ and then continues at the constant speed it has reached. Car $B$ accelerates uniformly at $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $8\text{ s}$ and then continues at the constant speed it has reached.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum speed reached by each car, and calculate the distance each car travels during its acceleration phase.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the time taken for the cars to pass each other, and find the distance from $P$ where they meet.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ moves along a straight horizontal track with constant speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $4\text{ s}$ after $A$ passes a fixed point $O$, particle $B$ passes through $O$ moving along the same track in the same direction. Particle $B$ passes $O$ with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and has a constant deceleration of $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Let $t$ be the time in seconds after $B$ passes through $O$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find expressions, in terms of $t$, for the displacement from $O$ of each particle, and find the two values of $t$ at which the particles are at the same point.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the time at which particle $B$ has its maximum lead over particle $A$, and calculate this maximum distance.

questions.prompt: Two runners, Leo and Max, compete along a straight track. Leo accelerates uniformly from rest for $4\text{ s}$ at $a\text{ m s}^{-2}$, maintains the speed he has reached for $8\text{ s}$, and then decelerates to rest uniformly over $4\text{ s}$. Max accelerates uniformly from rest, reaching a speed of $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in a distance of $18\text{ m}$. He maintains this speed for $8\text{ s}$, and then decelerates to rest uniformly over $4\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that $a = 1.5$, find which runner travels further, and calculate the difference in the total distances covered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the value of $a$ for which both runners cover the same total distance.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ moves along a straight line at a constant speed of $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When $P$ passes a fixed mark $O$, particle $Q$ is at $O$ at rest. At time $t = 0$ (the instant $P$ passes $O$), particle $Q$ begins to accelerate at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for $8\text{ s}$, reaching speed $V$, and then immediately decelerates uniformly at $1\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until coming to rest.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed $V$ of particle $Q$, and find the distance between $P$ and $Q$ at the end of the acceleration phase ($t = 8\text{ s}$).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that particle $Q$ never overtakes particle $P$, and find the minimum distance between the two particles during their motion.

questions.prompt: A truck passes a checkpoint $C$ travelling along a straight highway at a constant speed of $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $5\text{ s}$ later, a car starts from rest at $C$ and accelerates uniformly at $2.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until reaching a speed of $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The car then continues at this constant speed. Let $t$ be the time in seconds elapsed since the car started from $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the time taken for the car to reach its top speed of $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the distance travelled by the car during this acceleration phase, and the separation distance between the two vehicles at this instant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total time elapsed from the car's departure until it overtakes the truck, and calculate the total distance travelled by the car to the overtaking point.

questions.prompt: Two cars, $A$ and $B$, are travelling towards each other along a straight single-lane road. Car $A$ is travelling at $22\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and Car $B$ is travelling at $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When the distance between the two cars is $170\text{ m}$, both drivers simultaneously observe the danger. Each driver has a reaction time of $0.5\text{ s}$ before applying the brakes, which produce a constant deceleration of $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ on each car.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total stopping distance required for each car from the instant the danger is observed, and show that a collision is inevitable.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine the time $t$ elapsed from the instant danger is observed until the collision occurs, and find the speed of each car at the instant of impact.
